title: Check if Move is Legal
summary: Given an 8x8 grid board where free cells are marked '.', white cells are marked 'W', and black cells are marked 'B', determine if changing a free cell at position (rMove, cMove) to the specified color (either white or black) results in a good line.
statement: Given an 8x8 grid board where free cells are marked '.', white cells are marked 'W', and black cells are marked 'B', determine if changing a free cell at position (rMove, cMove) to the specified color (either white or black) results in a good line. A good line is defined as a sequence of three or more cells where the cells at the endpoints are of the same color, and all cells in between are of the opposite color. Return true if the move is legal, or false if it is not.
constraints: board is exactly 8 by 8 and contains '.', 'B', and 'W'.
The selected row and column are in range and currently contain '.'.
A legal move must form a straight line in one of eight directions with at least one opposite-color piece between the new piece and an existing piece of color.
hints: A move is legal if any one of the eight rays starts with one or more opponent pieces and ends at your color before leaving the board or reaching a gap.
Walk each direction from the move, count consecutive opponent cells, then check for an in-bounds same-color endpoint.
For each nonzero (dr,dc): advance through other color; accept when count>0 and the next cell equals color.
The scan tests every possible straight line through the new piece. Requiring an opponent run and same-color endpoint is exactly the good-line definition.
editorial: The scan tests every possible straight line through the new piece. Requiring an opponent run and same-color endpoint is exactly the good-line definition.
